citation: Leskovec, Lang, Dasgupta, Mahoney. Community Structure in Large Networks: Natural Cluster Sizes and the Absence of Large Well-Defined Clusters. Internet Mathematics 6(1), 29-123, 2009.

rules.sampling: BFS from minimum original ID, ascending original neighbors; nested prefixes 20/200/2000; all induced edges retained.
rules.exits: Boundary nodes only; start with minimum original ID, then farthest from current exits; ties by original ID. Count=min(boundary count, nodes//20).
rules.ingress: All non-exit nodes in BFS order; round-robin assignment of original A arrival order. Trips originate throughout the sampled area.
rules.direction: Original edges with exit distance decreasing by exactly one; same-level edges omitted.
rules.workload: Native Poisson A arrivals, inclusive interval 0..H-1; preserve IDs and times; replace placeholder work with ingress distance+1.
rules.demand: No-loss uniform-ingress flow split equally on outgoing edges; bottleneck arrival capacity=4/max(node visit fraction). Pressure targets 0.5/1/1.5; H=ceil(target/nominal rate), lambda=target/H.
rules.resources: 4 servers, 20 waiting spaces, Sub-1 duration 1. Exact total server percentages; reductions remove servers in BFS-order rounds.

feasibility.method: Per-demand pilot raw ZIP size and runtime scaled by final target/pilot realized jobs; 3 low + 21 stressed + 3 overloaded per scale. Excludes analysis copies, native C outputs, plots and inputs; ZIP ratios and runtime may change.
feasibility.peak_memory: Not measured. Full-size accounting and C memory costs remain to be checked before large batches.
